title: Isolation Debug Mode and the Network Latency window: what they do, capture and export

prose.label: Debug Mode.
prose.text: {{debug-start}} {{debug-stop-timeout}} {{debug-zip}} {{debug-general-information}} The ZIP password is set in the profile: [[zbi.isolation-profiles:debug-mode-zip-password]]. One ZIP field is not defined {{gap:ectx-field}}.

checks.do: Whether Debug Mode was started, which terminates and restarts the session and closes the other tabs.
Whether the latency statistics were exported and sent to Zscaler Support.

debug-start.statement: Starting Debug Mode terminates the current isolation session and restarts it with debug mode active; only the selected tab enters debug mode, the other tabs of the session close with their information lost, and tabs opened afterwards are automatically in debug mode.

quotes: notes that the current isolation session will be terminated to begin a new one.
only the selected tab enters debug mode. The other tabs in the existing session close automatically, and any information on those tabs is lost when the session restarts.
If you open new tabs while in the restarted isolated session, the new tabs are automatically in debug mode.

debug-stop-timeout.statement: Debug mode deactivates by itself after a timeout of 10 minutes if not stopped manually; data is still captured if the isolation session ends during debug mode, and stopping with several tabs open captures data from all tabs.

quotes: If you do not manually stop debug mode, it deactivates after a timeout period of 10 minutes.
If you end your isolation session while using debug mode, all data from the debugging is still captured.
If you stop debug mode when there are multiple tabs open, the data from all tabs is captured.

debug-zip.statement: When debug mode ends a ZIP file named debug_DDMMYY: TimeinUTC, encrypted with a password set by the admin, is generated and downloaded; it holds console logs, HAR data, netlog data, network latency information and general Zscaler information.

quotes: The ZIP file is named in the format debug_DDMMYY: TimeinUTC and is encrypted by a password set by the admin.
Console Logs: Information from the website(s) accessed while in isolation.
HTTP Archive format (HAR) Data: Information about the isolated session.
Netlog Data: Information from the web browser used.
Network Latency: Information from the isolation network diagnostics tab.
General Information: Information that pertains to Zscaler, such as:

debug-general-information.statement: The General Information part of the debug ZIP includes the isolation profile name and ID, the Internet & SaaS or Private Access tenant ID, the isolation tenant ID, isolation region and cluster information, the isolation browser egress IP address, the Internet & SaaS PAC file, any modified PAC file, flow details and correlation IDs.

quotes: Isolation profile name and ID
Isolation region and cluster information
Isolation browser egress IP address
Internet & SaaS PAC file
Modified PAC file (if applicable)
Flow details (Internet & SaaS Flow/IdP Proxy Flow/Private Access Flow)
Correlation IDs (endpoint session ID, pod ID, etc.)
Internet & SaaS (ZIA) or Private Access (ZPA) tenant ID (including the cloud name)
Isolation tenant ID

debug-purpose.statement: Debug Mode lets an end user troubleshoot whether an issue relates to the isolated session itself, without revealing confidential information.

quotes: This allows users to decipher whether the issue occurring is related to the isolated session itself or something else related to their web browsing.
Debug Mode allows users to troubleshoot the issue without revealing confidential information.
An end user of Zero Trust Browser, however, cannot see these details that are typically available in the native browser.

network-latency-window.statement: The Network Latency window shows live, real-time latency statistics for WebSocket and HTTP connectivity: last value, number of pings, max, 99%, 75%, 50Mean and standard deviation.

quotes: This window has live, real-time statistics of network latency for WebSocket and HTTP connectivity.
Last value: The latency of the last ping
Number of pings: The total number of pings sent
Max: The highest latency logged
99%: 99% of pings have latency that is less than or equal to the indicated value (e.g., 133 ms).
75%: 75% of pings have latency that is less than or equal to the indicated value (e.g., 96 ms).
50Mean: 50% of pings have latency that is less than or equal to the indicated value (e.g., 94 ms).
Std. deviation: The variance in latency across pings

network-latency-export.statement: Export Logs in the Network Latency window saves the report to the device as a text file by default, which can be sent to Zscaler Support.

quotes: Click Export Logs. By default, the report is saved to your device as a text file.
you can save the information captured in the Network Latency window to share as a report with Zscaler Support

ectx-field.title: What the debug ZIP field Expected cooperative transmission count (ECTX) means
ectx-field.detail: The extraction report found a debug ZIP field named Expected cooperative transmission count (ECTX) that the debug article does not define; it links Accessing Network Diagnostics in Isolation, which is not captured under that title.
